title: Order state machine
skill: Hand over the whole table and every error

good: In orders/order.py add ALLOWED = {new: (paid, cancelled), paid: (packed, cancelled), packed: (shipped, cancelled), shipped: (delivered,), delivered: (), cancelled: ()}. Order.__init__ sets self.history = []. Add property is_final (no allowed moves) and transition(to): if to not in ALLOWED raise ValueError(f"unknown state: {to}"); if is_final raise InvalidTransition(f"order {self.id} is {self.status} and cannot change"); if to not in ALLOWED[status] raise InvalidTransition(f"cannot move order {self.id} from {self.status} to {to}"); else append the tuple (status, to) to history and set status. Make pay/pack/ship/deliver/cancel each just call self.transition(<state>). In orders/service.py: cancel_all wraps order.cancel() in try/except InvalidTransition and skips failures; ship_ready ships only status == "packed". Do not change tests/ or errors.py. Then run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
lazy: Turn Order into a proper state machine so invalid moves are rejected.
